default_prompt: You are screening a record for a systematic review on the pharmacokinetics of emicizumab. Read the title and abstract and decide whether the record should be included, applying this review's published eligibility criteria (SYNERGY dataset; original review DOI 10.1007/s40262-021-01042-w): the following inclusion criteria were applied: emicizumab studies providing (1) data on humans, (2) original PK data or modeled PK data or PK/PD relationships, and (3) access to the abstract and the full text in English.
_notes: One of 4 per-review config files (runbook §2, §6), but the ONLY one at x = 5 --
see reviews/README.md's 'vendors (x = 5, Donners_2021 only)' and 'tau' sections for
why this review alone diverges from the shared x = 4 instrument used by
van_de_Schoot_2018/Appenzeller-Herzog_2019/Muthu_2021. anthropic/openai/google/mistral
here are byte-identical to those three reviews' vendor blocks (the shared instrument
is unchanged); only 'openmodel' and 'tau' are new for this file specifically.
default_prompt verified against source (2026-08-25): fetched asreview/synergy-dataset's
actual datasets.toml from GitHub (gh api repos/asreview/synergy-dataset/contents/
datasets.toml) and copied Donners_2021's 'eligibility_criteria' word for word after
the instruction/DOI framing. DOI 10.1007/s40262-021-01042-w; 258 records, 15 included
(~5.8%) per synergy-dataset v1.2 -- re-confirm with `synergy_dataset show Donners_2021`
before a real run if a newer package/dataset version is in use.
'openmodel' is attest's generic self-hosted/OpenAI-compatible-endpoint vendor factory
(attest.vendors.registry._build_openmodel) -- there is no dedicated 'alexandra' vendor
factory in the kernel. 'Alexandra' names the Alexandra Institute, who host this
particular openmodel deployment (qwen3.5-397b); the vendor key in this file is
'openmodel', matching every other openmodel user of the kernel.
base_url is 'https://inference.alexandra.dk/v1', NOT the full
'https://inference.alexandra.dk/v1/chat/completions' recorded in this repo's own
gitignored .env (ALEX_URL) -- attest.vendors.providers.openmodel.OpenModelRater appends
'/chat/completions' itself, so passing the full path here would double it. base_url is
hash-versioned (attest.provenance.config.VendorSpec.base_url) since a different serving
stack behind the same nominal model name is exactly the drift model_version/
check_model_version exists to catch, so it is a literal in this file, not env-sourced.
api_key_env is 'ALEX_API_KEY' (real key lives only in the gitignored .env, added
there directly by the user, not by this session) -- deliberately excluded from
to_dict()/ensemble_config_id (VendorSpec.api_key_env docstring): it names where the
secret lives, not a value that changes what the vendor samples. Requires kernel commit
0d52a20 or later (base_url/api_key_env added to VendorSpec) -- confirmed this repo's
own .venv is bumped to commit 747e5b7 (also picks up the companion validation commit
that rejects base_url/api_key_env on vendors that don't consume them).
reasoning_effort: 'none' on openmodel, mirroring openai's gpt-5.6-terra treatment --
per attest.vendors.providers.openmodel.OpenModelRater's own docstring, confirmed live
against this exact qwen3.5-397b/Alexandra Institute endpoint on 2026-08-25:
reasoning_effort='none' disables a hidden reasoning phase outright (cutting completion
tokens for a single-letter answer from roughly 950 to 2), while 'low'/'medium'/'high'
were all indistinguishable from each other and from omitting the field -- i.e. this
endpoint exposes no graduated effort control, only on/off. This also keeps
OpenModelRater's own max_tokens default (8, not configurable via VendorSpec/config.json
-- see registry._build_openmodel) sufficient: at that same default, the endpoint's
hidden reasoning phase alone was previously confirmed to starve `content` to empty
when reasoning was NOT disabled.
temperature: 0.0 on openmodel is the same requested value as anthropic/mistral, for the
same determinism rationale (reviews/README.md's 'temperature' section) -- but, unlike
every other vendor in this ensemble, NOT yet confirmed live against a real call to this
endpoint (only reasoning_effort has been). send_temperature is left at its default
(true, i.e. temperature is sent) since nothing has shown this endpoint rejects an
explicit temperature -- re-verify before freezing a real run, the same way
anthropic/openai/google's temperature handling above was each confirmed live rather
than assumed.
tau = 0.497468076502562, re-derived for x = 5 (NOT copied from the other three
reviews' x = 4 tau -- reviews/README.md's 'tau' section: tau is not comparable across
ensemble sizes). attest.ensemble.tau.resolve_tau's TIE_POLICY_ESCALATE only accepts an
even x (a 'clean tie' requires splitting votes exactly in half), so it cannot be called
directly at x = 5. Generalized by hand, using the same kernel-verified
attest.ensemble.tau.reachable_dispersions(5) the kernel itself uses: the three
attainable non-boundary dispersions at x = 5 are 0.0 (5-0/0-5 unanimous), ~0.4472
(4-1/1-4), and ~0.5477 (3-2/2-3, the closest-to-even split and, not coincidentally,
the maximum reachable value -- the same property TIE_POLICY_ESCALATE's even-x 'tie'
combo always has). tau is the midpoint of the two largest, (0.4472135954999579 +
0.5477225575051661) / 2, i.e. escalate only a 3-2 split, auto-label 4-1 and 5-0 --
the direct x = 5 analog of x = 4's 'escalate a 2-2 tie, auto-label a 3-1 majority'.
Re-checked with attest.ensemble.tau.describe_tau(tau, x=5): zero warnings, canonical
interval (0.4472135954999579, 0.5477225575051661) -- this value is not on a reachable
point and not confusable with any other regime. attest.ensemble.tau.validate_tau
still re-derives and checks this tau against x = 5 automatically at `attest screen`
epoch-open time, same as every other review's tau.
This file is not read literally beyond 'vendors' (including each vendor's
'temperature'), 'aggregation', 'tau', 'batch_size', 'zero_policy', 'default_prompt',
'track_prompts' (unused here), and 'confidence_threshold' (see
attest.cli._load_ensemble_config) -- this _notes field is ignored by the loader and
safe to keep as documentation.
'batch_size' is 1, same rationale as every other review -- see
reviews/README.md's batch_size section, not repeated here.
